title: Explicit native file permissions block misspelled candidates without disabling atomic writes
observation: Channel Absmax Scale Turn13 successfully wrote ccandidate-set.py twice and the correct file once; v4 correctly refused. An OS-read-only-directory probe also blocked the correct native atomic Write, so that route is rejected. Claude2.1.226 default permission mode with exact absolute Write/Edit rules refused both a misspelled leaf and a nested candidate, while correct Write/Read/Edit succeeded and left only candidate-set.py. The denied attempts have matching tool invocation, native notice, errored completion and terminal declaration.
proposed_change: Opt-in v6 uses the existing OS-isolated wrapper, default permission mode and exact file rules on initial/resumed invocations. It preserves all denial witnesses and requires successful canonical writes. Earlier contracts and sealed Runs retain their semantics. A bounded dispatcher may continue after an archived, replayed, named author path fault; custody, unknown provider/account and device failures stop submissions. No failed Run is retried or counted as success.
promotion_disposition: Lab authoring and dispatch protocol only; no Compiler or performance promotion. CPU fixture tests and fresh native initial/resume qualification gate successor experiments.
